extracted.intended_audience: typefounders, printers, typographers, book designers, compositors
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and presenting printed type specimens showing a typeface family in multiple sizes, styles, scripts, and uses so printers/designers can evaluate the face. Emphasizes point sizes, weights/variants, leading (solid vs leaded), language/script samples, figures, special characters, and labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font family / face name
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and display the name of the typeface family (e.g., CASLON OLD STYLE, SCOTCH ROMAN, BOOKMAN OLD STYLE, CHELTENHAM, CLARENDON, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the family name prominently near the specimen (as on the page: CASLON OLD STYLE, SCOTCH ROMAN, BOOKMAN OLD STYLE, etc.). Use the family name as the heading for each specimen block so the reader immediately knows which face is being shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the specimen at explicit point sizes, labelled (e.g., SIX POINT, EIGHT POINT, TEN POINT, TWELVE POINT, FOURTEEN POINT, EIGHTEEN POINT, TWENTY-TWO POINT, TWENTY-FOUR POINT, THIRTY-SIX POINT, FORTY-EIGHT POINT, SIXTY POINT, SEVENTY-TWO POINT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a range of sizes from small text sizes (6–9 pt) up through display sizes (30–72 pt) with each size labelled so readers can compare how the face performs at each point size. The page repeatedly groups identical sample copy under a size heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting/leading indication (Solid vs [Leaded])
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the specimen is set 'Solid' or with 'Leaded' line spacing (e.g., [Leaded], [Solid]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly show the line-setting used for the specimen so readers can judge vertical spacing and legibility. The page marks specimens with [Leaded] or [Solid] adjacent to the point-size heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style/variant display (italic, bold, condensed, extended, wide, bold condensed, bold italic, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show different face variants and weights for the family (italic, italic caps, italic body, condensed, condensed bold, bold, bold italic, extended, wide, condensed italic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide separate specimen blocks for each variant (e.g., CHELTENHAM OLD STYLE ITALIC, CHELTENHAM WIDE, CHELTENHAM CONDENSED, CHELTENHAM BOLD, CHELTENHAM BOLD ITALIC). Label the variant clearly so users can compare forms and weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample paragraph text
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a repeatable prose passage as body-text sample (the page repeatedly uses 'When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius saw the fall of Carthage and of Corinth...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a realistic paragraph of body text to demonstrate metrics, texture, and readability. The specimen also shows the same paragraph across sizes/variants to permit direct comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display caps / headline lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Include display (all-caps) lines for headline/display use (e.g., 'THE FIRST TIME THAT THE GRAND PROSPECT HAD BEEN HELD FORTH').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show uppercase display settings in addition to body text to illustrate how capitals, spacing, and overall color work for headings and titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals / figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Show sequences of numerals and label figure sets (e.g., '1234567890', 'SEVEN POINT FIGURES').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present numerals at the same sizes as text samples, and include dedicated lines of figures so readers can assess numeral design, weight, and spacing at different point sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous signs / punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a block of miscellaneous symbols and punctuation marks (the page has a 'MISCELLANEOUS SIGNS' section showing = + - × ÷ ± : ; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a set of common typographic signs so users can inspect glyphs used in mathematical notation, operators, bullets, and punctuation. Present them across sizes where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accented letters and diacritics
rubrics_metrics.description: Show accented letters across relevant sizes (labelled 'ACCENTED LETTERS — SIX TO TWELVE POINT').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include accented characters and typical diacritic combinations for languages that require them, especially at small text sizes (6–12pt) to verify legibility and diacritic placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Latin script samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specimens for other scripts/languages (e.g., PORSON GREEK, ANTIQUE GREEK, INSCRIPTION GREEK, HEBREW, NESTORIAN SYRIAC, ARABIC, ETHIOPIC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show complete script samples and relevant sizes for each supported script so users can assess language-specific letterforms, diacritics, and overall rhythm. Label the script and point sizes as done on the page (e.g., 'PORSON GREEK — SIX POINT').

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters / sample character repertoire
rubrics_metrics.description: Display special characters and language-specific glyphs (accented letters, ligatures, punctuation, special marks) and indicate 'SPECIAL CHARACTERS — ALL SIZES' where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the full repertoire (accents, ligatures, ornaments, special punctuation) so buyers/typographers can confirm availability and design consistency across sizes and styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen labeling and publisher attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Label specimens with the family, size, variant, and often the printer/publisher imprint (e.g., 'THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO PRESS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear headings and an identifying imprint or credit line to contextualize the specimen; headings commonly show family name and point-size/variant, and occasional publisher header appears on specimen pages.
